chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for he said: 'Whoever opens for himself a door of begging, Allah opens for him a door of poverty.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of habitual begging according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, highlights the continuity between the Prophet’s teachings and the Imams’ guidance, specifically warning against the spiritual danger of habitual begging (*mas'alah*). In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as physical poverty but as a state of spiritual destitution resulting from excessive dependence on others, contrasting with the virtue of self-sufficiency (*istighna*). The warning serves as a practical ethical guideline for maintaining dignity and independence in social and economic interactions.
